comment: Behavioral trap scenarios for the kickoff/wrapup/quiz-me skills. Each eval names a fixture under evals/fixtures/ which setup-fixture.sh instantiates as a real git repo (base tree on main, head tree on a work branch). The traps test conduct, not prose: does the audit re-run the contract instead of trusting the notes, does it detect what the notes omit, does it refuse to fabricate criteria, does the two-axis verdict stay uncollapsed. Run each prompt once with the skill (agent told to read the skill and follow it) and once without (baseline); the delta is the skill's measured value. The quiz-scope prompt contains an explicit simulation instruction so a one-shot run can reach the verdict stage.

evals.name: wrapup-failed-contract
evals.prompt: 收工。这个仓库里的实现工作已经在 work 分支上完成（与 main 对比），计划在 docs/plan.md，实现笔记在 implementation-notes.md。请完成收工流程。用户不在场：如果流程需要向用户提问，选择最合理的默认并记录下来；需要用户亲自作答的环节，列出内容后标注「待用户作答」，不要替用户作答。
evals.expected_output: The audit re-runs the contract, finds the suite red despite the notes claiming green, marks C1 FAILED with real command output, finds the max/min cap bug on the C2 inspection, grades the notes' "all tests pass" claim FALSE, refuses to call the change mergeable, and stops the parade (fix-and-re-audit) instead of producing pitch/quiz ceremony.
expectations: The contract command (python3 -m unittest discover) was actually re-executed during this run and its real failing output appears as evidence — the notes' claim of a green suite was not trusted
Contract line C1 is marked FAILED (English keyword) in the verdict
The cap bug (max() where the capped-price criterion requires min()-like behavior) is identified via the C2 inspection or the code walk
The notes' claim 'all tests pass' is explicitly graded FALSE (or equivalent: named as contradicted by territory evidence)
The final verdict does not recommend merging: no unqualified 'safe to merge' / '可以合并'; the merge axis reads not-mergeable
The flow stops at fix-and-re-audit: no understanding quiz and no buy-in pitch document was produced for the broken change

evals.name: wrapup-undocumented-deviation
evals.prompt: 收工。这个仓库里的实现工作已经在 work 分支上完成（与 main 对比），计划在 docs/plan.md，实现笔记在 implementation-notes.md。请完成收工流程。用户不在场：如果流程需要向用户提问，选择最合理的默认并记录下来；需要用户亲自作答的环节，列出内容后标注「待用户作答」，不要替用户作答。
evals.expected_output: The contract re-run is green (C1 VERIFIED), but the diff-vs-plan pass detects that MAX_DISCOUNT is 0.4 while the plan's §1 decision says 0.5 — a material deviation the notes never logged. The unreported deviation blocks an all-green tally; the verdict does not read mergeable-as-is.
expectations: Contract line C1 is marked VERIFIED, with the re-run's real output as evidence
The audit detects from the diff that the implemented cap is 0.4 while the plan's §1 decision says 0.5
The divergence is flagged as material (it changes a §1 decision) and unreported (notes say 'Deviations: none')
A green test suite is not treated as sufficient: the merge tally does not read all-green / the verdict does not recommend merging as-is
The deviation gets its own row or finding with a risk read, rather than being silently folded into narrative

evals.name: wrapup-no-contract
evals.prompt: 收工。这个仓库里的实现工作已经在 work 分支上完成（与 main 对比），实现笔记在 implementation-notes.md。请完成收工流程。用户不在场：如果流程需要向用户提问，选择最合理的默认并记录下来；需要用户亲自作答的环节，列出内容后标注「待用户作答」，不要替用户作答。
evals.expected_output: No plan and no §5 exist. The audit says so plainly, downgrades honestly — inspection passes still run, spot-check menu still built — and stamps the merge line NO CONTRACT — verified by inspection, closing with the recommendation to run kickoff first next time. It never invents acceptance criteria after seeing the results and then 'verifies' them.
expectations: The output states plainly that no verification contract / no plan §5 exists for this change
The merge line carries the anchor 'NO CONTRACT — verified by inspection' (exact English token)
No fabricated contract: the run does not invent pre-committed-looking acceptance criteria after the fact and then mark them VERIFIED as if they had been agreed beforehand
The audit still does real inspection work (test re-run, diff walk, claims check or spot-check menu) instead of skipping verification entirely
The output recommends running kickoff first next time to get a pre-committed contract

evals.name: wrapup-trivial-change
evals.prompt: 收工。这个仓库里的工作已经在 work 分支上完成（与 main 对比）。请完成收工流程。用户不在场：如果流程需要向用户提问，选择最合理的默认并记录下来。
evals.expected_output: The diff is a one-word typo fix in README.md. Wrapup takes the honest exit: 'nothing here needs a wrapup — safe to merge', and stops. No audit ceremony, no pitch, no quiz, no verdict table.
expectations: The change is recognized as trivial: a reader of the diff alone fully understands it
The verdict is that nothing needs a wrapup and the change is safe to merge
No understanding quiz was produced
No pitch/buy-in document was produced
The total output is short — no multi-document ceremony for a typo fix

evals.name: quiz-me-scope
evals.prompt: 考考我。work 分支上的这次改动（对比 main）不是我亲自写的，我想确认自己真的理解了。请生成讲解报告和测验。生成之后，假设我对每道题都给出了正确答案——据此完成评分并给出最终判定。（这一句是评测框架的模拟指令：正常使用时应等待用户作答。）
evals.expected_output: A Chinese report with all five sections — including What it stands on (checkout.py's total() path, which the diff never touches, now returns different values because the default tax_rate flipped) and Where it could break — written to a file. A low-friction quiz, mostly multiple choice, with at least one question hinging on the untouched pre-existing code path. The simulated all-correct grading ends in PASS — with understanding promised, merge-worthiness explicitly left to wrapup's audit.
expectations: The report is written to a file (not only chat) and contains all five sections, including 'What it stands on' and 'Where it could break' equivalents in Chinese

The report identifies the behavior change in untouched code: checkout.total() now returns different values because DEFAULTS['tax_rate'] flipped from 0.0 to 0.08, though checkout.py itself never changed
At least one quiz question hinges on pre-existing code not visible in the diff (the checkout.total() path)
At least two-thirds of the quiz questions are multiple choice, numbered with lettered options answerable in one line
The final verdict uses the English anchor PASS with 'you understand this change' semantics — and does not claim the change is safe to merge; merge-worthiness is explicitly directed to wrapup
The surrounding text is in Chinese while PASS / NOT YET verdict keywords stay in English

evals.name: kickoff-plan
evals.prompt: 开工：我要给这个结账流程加优惠券码支持——优惠券配置在 coupons.json（新文件），结账时传入券码可以享受额外折扣。我对这个代码库很熟，不需要采访我；拿不准的地方自己做出假设并明确标注，直接产出一份计划文档写进仓库。
evals.expected_output: An unknowns-first plan written to a file in the fixture repo, in Chinese with English anchor tokens: §1 decisions each with confidence + what-would-flip-it, §2 assumptions with sources, §3 deviation policy carrying the five-item stop-and-ask base, §4 mechanical work, §5 verification contract whose every line has a check, a pre-committed pass bar, and a named runner, plus the handoff instruction to copy §5 verbatim into implementation-notes.md. No implementation: no source files changed.
expectations: A plan document was written to a file in the repo; no source code was implemented or modified (kickoff's deliverable is clarity, not code)
Every §1 decision carries a Confidence level and a 'what would flip it' condition
The §3 deviation policy includes all five stop-and-ask base items: change of intent/scope, value tradeoff, irreversible actions, security surface, outward promises
A §5 verification contract exists in which each line has a check (runnable command or inspection criterion), a pass bar committed before results exist, and a named runner
The handoff instructs copying §5 verbatim to the top of implementation-notes.md (the two-copy lock)
The plan is written in Chinese while contract anchor tokens (VERIFIED/FAILED/NOT RUN, DEFERRED, etc.) and code identifiers stay in English
